Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs LLMCo & FastServe

Hi Sofia / Rajiv —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to make the bake-off next week run smoothly. I’ve copied the internal team so we can move quickly on the items below.

Top pain points you shared
- Latency at peak: 95th percentile spikes >400ms on current setup
- Unit inference cost: high spend on per-token pricing, looking for ~40% reduction
- Security & audit: SOC 2 + strict data residency controls required for pilot
- Integration: need SSO + SCIM and easy model version pinning for rollout

Goals for the bake-off / decision criteria
1) Peak 95th latency <200ms for our 8k prompt workloads
2) Total cost per 1M tokens < $X (see test plan)
3) Support for private deployment (VPC) or dedicated tenancy
4) Clear observability: token-level cost + error traces
5) Security evidence: SOC2 report + KMS/HSM integration details

Open questions we noted
- How Redwood handles KV cache reuse across sessions for chat-style workloads
- Fallback behavior when dedicated capacity is exhausted
- Quantization/precision tradeoffs for our LLMs and expected perf delta

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Redwood: send bake-off test plan and pricing sheet (Marissa) — by EOD today
- NovaNet: confirm procurement & security attendees for kickoff — Rajiv to confirm by Tue
- Run perf/quality tests using NovaNet test harness next Wed (9/1) — both sides

Attachments: I’m sending a short test plan and our pricing summary in the next message. I’ve also uploaded a recording of today’s demo to the shared Drive link below.

Thanks again — excited to run this.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
